summary: Fixed F-001 from 003-T36-tests-result.json: apps/cli/src/runtime/inbound.test.ts:324 ('commits outbound plaintext history with native state/outbox before send and rolls all three back on persistence failure') asserted that a snapshot of alice's native store (session:/inbox:/outbox:/pre:/used: prefixes) taken BEFORE any publish or send attempt equals a snapshot taken AFTER a send() that fails via an injected persistence error. Established the property by reading the test end to end: the test's actual subject is that a persistence failure inside send()'s own commit rolls back exactly what send() itself attempted to write (session establishment, outbox entry, history entry) and nothing else - it is an atomicity/no-partial-write pin, not a claim that send() as a whole is a no-op on the store. Under T31's pool, send()'s first step is publish(), which durably mints alice's own 20-member first-contact prekey pool as N=20 separate already-committed transactions before send() ever runs; that write is real, legitimate, and outside the transaction under test, so comparing against a pre-publish baseline conflated it with the rollback being pinned. The old baseline was a coincidence of pool size 1, not the property. Did not touch the pool-size literal, since the property has nothing to do with a count. Instead expressed the assertion as before/after around the operation under test: added an optional afterPublish hook to the file's shared send() test helper (used only by this test; every other call site leaves the new parameter undefined, so no other test's behavior changed), invoked immediately after messenger.publish() resolves and before messenger.send() runs, and used it to capture the native-store snapshot at exactly that point. The final assertion now compares the post-failure snapshot against that post-publish/pre-send snapshot instead of against a pre-publish one. This form is independent of LIMITS.PREKEY_MIN_COUNT or any pool size, present or future, since it never encodes a count - it pins the invariant directly via a same-run before/after comparison. Verified the corrected assertion actually exercises the rollback: session:, inbox:, outbox: and used: are all empty in both snapshots and pre: holds the full published pool unchanged in both, so the comparison still meaningfully proves session/outbox/history atomicity, it does not pass vacuously. No product file, no documentation file, and no file other than inbound.test.ts was changed.

acceptance.criterion: Established what property the failing assertion at inbound.test.ts:324 actually protects, rather than only patching the arithmetic
acceptance.evidence: Read the whole test ('commits outbound plaintext history with native state/outbox before send and rolls all three back on persistence failure', inbound.test.ts:318-351) plus the shared send() helper (lines 49-81) and failCommitOnce() (lines 116-127). The test injects a commit failure gated on the first transaction touching cli:outbox: keys, calls send() (which internally does publish() then send()), and expects: (a) observedSend (the /v1/messages/send beforeAccept hook) was never called, i.e. no HTTP send happened; (b) the native store snapshot after the failed send equals a baseline; (c) cli:outbox: and cli:history: are empty afterward. Read T31's implementation report (t31-implementation-report.md, section 1.1) confirming publish() now mints the pool via mintPublicationSlot, which 'stores the member durably before it can be offered to anyone' - i.e. as its own committed transaction(s), unrelated to and preceding the transaction failCommitOnce targets. Concluded the property is: a persistence failure inside send()'s own outbox-touching transaction rolls back exactly what that transaction wrote (session establishment + outbox entry + history entry) and nothing beyond it - not that send() as a whole leaves the store byte-identical to its state before send() was ever invoked, since send() legitimately writes durable pool material via publish() first.

acceptance.criterion: Expressed the assertion in a form that survives the pool (before/after comparison or invariant, not a re-baselined literal)
acceptance.evidence: Added `afterPublish?: () => Promise<void>` as a 5th, optional parameter to the shared send() helper (inbound.test.ts), invoked as `await afterPublish?.();` immediately after `await messenger.publish();` and before `await messenger.send(...)`. In the target test, passed a callback that captures `beforeSend = await snapshot(alice, nativePrefixes)` at that point, then compares the post-failure snapshot against `beforeSend` instead of a pre-publish `before`. This encodes no count anywhere - not LIMITS.PREKEY_MIN_COUNT, not a literal - so it is unaffected by any future change to the pool's target size. Every other call site of send() in the file (10 other invocations) passes no 5th argument, so afterPublish is undefined there and their behavior is byte-identical to before this change.

The assertion is still an exact `.toEqual()` over the full nativePrefixes snapshot (session:, inbox:, outbox:, pre:, used:), not narrowed to a subset of prefixes, not loosened to toMatchObject/toContain/a length check, and not deleted. It still fails if session:, inbox:, outbox: or used: gain or lose any key, or if pre: changes at all between the two snapshot points - the only change is which two points are compared. Confirmed non-vacuous by inspection: at the afterPublish point pre: holds the full 20-member pool and session:/inbox:/outbox:/used: are empty; after the failed send those must still be empty and pre: must still hold exactly those same 20 members for the comparison to pass, which is exactly the rollback property being pinned.

acceptance.criterion: Any derived count uses LIMITS.PREKEY_MIN_COUNT, never a literal
acceptance.evidence: The corrected form makes no count comparison at all - it compares two runtime-captured store snapshots to each other, so there is no count to derive or hardcode.
